topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the learning objectives for the session on cancer causation.

topics.label: Origins and Drivers of Cancer: Genetics, Bad Luck, and the Environment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and examine the evidence balancing intrinsic biological errors, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, using the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma as an illustrative case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific physical mutagens and metabolically activated chemicals cause direct DNA damage and bulky adduct formation across various tissues.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Cellular Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics contrast direct mutagens with tumor promoters to explain how chronic inflammation, aberrant signaling pathways, and tissue developmental timing drive clonal expansion.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the mutational signature analyses, epidemiological tools, in vivo animal models, and in vitro bioassays used to establish carcinogenic risk.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing key concepts and framing carcinogen exposure within everyday risk-benefit decision-making.
